top_story: After months of brinkmanship that peaked in March with US threats against Iran’s power grid and Tehran’s warnings of wider regional retaliation, Washington and Tehran now appear set to sign a deal in Switzerland on Friday that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The shift sharply lowers the immediate risk of a Gulf escalation that had threatened shipping, energy flows, and civilian infrastructure across the region. That de-escalatory turn does not extend to Gaza, where Israel’s intensified campaign as of 9 June has deepened mass civilian harm and reinforced a regional pattern in which diplomatic relief in one arena coexists with severe violence in another. The emerging picture is of a Middle East entering a more stable phase around the Gulf while the Palestinian theatre remains a central source of human and political volatility.
